title: Gender equality progress is advancing incrementally while leadership, budgeting, legal, digital, land, and bodily-agency gaps continue to limit power
source_unit: United Nations Statistics Division and UN Women, The Gender Snapshot 2026 / SDG Goal 5 progress report
geography: Global SDG Goal 5 indicators, national and local political institutions, workplaces, households, agricultural land systems, digital access, and reproductive-health agency

denominator.unit: global national-parliament, local-government, and managerial-position frame

women_national_parliament_share_2026.unit: percent of national parliamentary seats held by women as of 1 January 2026

women_local_government_share_2025.unit: percent of local-government positions held by women in 2025

women_managerial_share_2025.unit: percent of managerial positions held by women worldwide in 2025

parliament_progress_since_2015.unit: percentage-point increase in women's share of national parliamentary seats since 2015

progress_since_2025.unit: percentage-point increase in women's share of national parliamentary seats since 2025

observations.method: UN SDG Goal 5 monitoring using global indicators on political representation, local government, and managerial positions.
observations.uncertainty: Representation shares do not establish agenda-setting power, portfolio control, policy responsiveness, workplace authority, or equal outcomes within gender groups.
observations.subgroup: Women candidates, elected officials, managers, workers, political parties, public institutions, employers, and households affected by gendered policy decisions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Incremental representation can still change recruitment, policy priorities, and institutional legitimacy; descriptive parity is not sufficient for power or accountability.

observations.period: 2018-2025; gender-responsive public finance and institutional accountability

denominator.unit: countries reporting systems to track and make public gender-equality allocations

countries_with_tracking_systems_2025.unit: countries reporting a system to track and allocate resources for gender equality in 2025

countries_with_tracking_systems_2018.unit: countries reporting such a system in 2018

comprehensive_system_share.unit: percent of countries with comprehensive systems to track and make public gender-equality allocations, approximately one in four

accountability_boundary.value: the presence of a tracking system does not establish adequate allocation, implementation, impact, or public accountability

observations.method: UN SDG Goal 5 monitoring of gender-responsive budgeting and public allocation-tracking systems.
observations.uncertainty: Country reporting systems vary in scope, transparency, quality, and use; system presence is not spending incidence or evidence that gender priorities shape outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Finance ministries, gender-equality institutions, civil society, public-service users, women and girls, legislators, auditors, and budget advocates.
observations.counterinterpretation: Even incomplete systems can improve visibility and create entry points for accountability; a comprehensive system may still fail without political commitment or implementation capacity.

observations.period: 2019-2026; legal rights, land security, and digital access

denominator.unit: global SDG Goal 5 legal, land, agricultural-household, and mobile-access indicators

legal_reforms_since_2019.unit: legal reforms reported as advancing women's rights since 2019

women_agricultural_land_rights.unit: percent-or-fewer of women in agricultural households reporting ownership or secure rights to agricultural land in 68 countries with data

women_without_mobile_phone_share.unit: percent of the population without mobile phones represented by women in 2025

mobile_ownership_gap.unit: percent women are less likely than men to own a mobile phone globally in 2025, approximately

observations.method: UN SDG Goal 5 synthesis of legal-reform tracking, agricultural land-rights indicators, and mobile-phone ownership data.
observations.uncertainty: Legal reform counts do not establish enforcement or lived access; land and mobile indicators vary by country, household, documentation, use, affordability, and safety.
observations.subgroup: Women in agricultural households, rural women, mobile-internet users, women seeking economic opportunity, legal institutions, and households with insecure land or device access.
observations.counterinterpretation: Legal reform and mobile diffusion can improve agency and opportunity when paired with enforcement, affordable access, digital safety, documentation, and social acceptance.

denominator.unit: countries with available data on women's reported reproductive-health decision-making

contraceptive_decision_agency.unit: percent of married or partnered women aged 15-49 reporting ability to make their own decisions about contraceptive use in 2025 data

reproductive_healthcare_agency.unit: percent of married or partnered women reporting similar agency in reproductive-healthcare decisions

refusal_of_sex_agency.unit: percent of married or partnered women reporting ability to refuse sex

cross_domain_boundary.value: reported agency differs across contraceptive use, healthcare, and ability to refuse sex and is not equivalent to service access, safety, or freedom from coercion

observations.method: UN SDG Goal 5 compilation of country data on reproductive-health decision-making among married or partnered women aged 15-49.
observations.uncertainty: Self-reported agency measures do not establish actual service availability, safety, coercion-free choice, partner dynamics, legal rights, or health outcomes; coverage is limited to countries with data.
observations.subgroup: Married or partnered women aged 15-49, reproductive-health providers, households, legal and health systems, and women facing unequal bargaining power or service access.
observations.counterinterpretation: High reported agency in one domain can coexist with constraints in another; improvements may come from services, information, legal reform, social norms, or measurement changes.

related_sources.claim: UN Women and UN DESA Gender Snapshot 2026 context on leadership, institutional power, and SDG progress.
Official UN SDG Goal 5 2026 monitoring page with representation, budgeting, legal, digital, land, and agency indicators.

boundary: This record adds a gender-accountability route from representation and legal reform through budget visibility, digital and land access, and bodily agency. It is aggregate SDG monitoring, not respondent-level causal analysis, proof of institutional power, individual legal enforcement, household bargaining, or health outcomes.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official UN SDG Goal 5 2026 page and related UN Women/UN DESA framing were reviewed; leadership, local government, managerial, budgeting, legal reform, land, mobile-access, and reproductive-agency claims were cross-checked.
